title: events: logfile: do not immediately stop tail when until is in the past
body:
<!-- Please include the 'why' behind your changes if no issue exists -->
### Fixes
Fixes #29579

### Description
When using `events_logger = "file"`, invoking `podman events` with `--until` set to a timestamp or duration in the past caused the logfile reader to stop immediately before historical events could be collected from the file.

This occurred because `time.Until(untilTime)` evaluates to a non-positive duration when `untilTime` is in the past, causing the background timer goroutine in `EventLogFile.Read` to immediately call `t.Stop()`, closing `t.Lines` concurrently during startup.

This PR checks `time.Until(untilTime) > 0` before launching the timer goroutine. Filtering for past events already continues to function accurately via `generateEventUntilOption` in `applyFilters`.

### Tests
- Added unit test `TestEventLogFileReadUntilInPast` in `libpod/events/logfile_test.go` verifying historical event reads when `--until` is in the past without streaming.
- Signed-off with DCO.

Signed-off-by: K J sundeep kumar <sundeep8967@gmail.com>
